title: Oriented trees and their finite-subtree zigzag diagram
statement: Let $V$ be a small set. An oriented tree $T$ on $V$ is a simple graph $G$ that is connected and acyclic, together with a relation $a\to b$ such that $G(a,b)$ if and only if $a\to b$ or $b\to a$, and $a\to b$ excludes $b\to a$. Its free path category $C_T$ has vertices $V$ and finite directed edge words as arrows. For $x\in V$, let $\mathcal F_x(T)$ be the inclusion poset of finite vertex subsets $S$ containing $x$ whose induced graph is connected. Write a finite signed word using $+$ and $-$, and use the relative zigzag categories and ordinary nerves of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] for the pair $(C_T,C_T)$. The subtree category $Z_w^{C_S}(x,x)$ is represented canonically inside $Z_w^{C_T}(x,x)$ by diagrams all of whose vertices belong to $S$, with the ambient commuting vertical diagrams as morphisms: connected subtrees of a tree contain every path between their vertices, so this is exactly the embedded free-path category construction, including empty and identity paths. Subset inclusions give functors retaining all diagram and path data. Their ordinary nerves form a diagram $\mathcal F_x(T)\to\mathbf{sSet}$, with the cocone of inclusions into $NZ_w^{C_T}(x,x)$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
